message.content: Painting the Eiffel Tower is a massive undertaking that’s carried out only when the structure needs a fresh coat of protective paint (usually every 7 years). In practice, the actual painting work—covering the entire lattice, applying multiple layers, and letting them cure—takes roughly **two months**. That’s the time spent on the tower itself; the overall project, including scaffolding, safety checks, and logistics, can extend over several weeks before and after the painting phase.
